name: Resolution sniping: outcome known, oracle not yet settled
one_line: Buy decided-but-unresolved or near-certain outcomes at 95-99.9c, recycle capital fast, and price long-dated certainties off an explicit settlement-discount curve.
scope: Cover ONLY the post-outcome window: the real-world result is known (or knowable from a primary feed) but the market has not settled. Go deep on what a sniping-bot builder underestimates: the measured gap from outcome to proposal to settlement by category, who still sells at 97-99.9c and why, how automatic / non-UMA resolution (Chainlink price feeds, sports data feeds, the US exchange) has shrunk the opportunity set, tick size and fee regime at price extremes, depth actually available, 'resolved-but-unsettled bonding' economics (median APY, top provider PnL, trade counts), dispute / too-early / clarification tail risk by category and how to size it, capital lock during disputes, first-to-know data sources, and competition. Boundary: PRE-outcome high-probability buying and holding-rewards carry are near-certain-bond-carry; trading the dispute itself is rules-dispute-trading; weather station-feed sniping is detailed in weather-markets (cross-reference).

parent_scope: Cover the turnover business (Certainty Harvester pattern: enter 0.95-0.999, sell at 0.99, dump losers at 0.001-0.005; 90% of >=$10k orders above 0.95), post-event bonding economics (median APY 6.22%, top provider $23,616 over 34,994 trades, 182 s median resolution-to-redemption), the settlement-wedge term structure (3-7% annualised, AAVE-correlated, neg-risk compression), near-zero tail fees under p(1-p), the thin gross edge (+0.83c per dollar at >=90c), reversal/dispute/slippage/gas failure data, time-value and liquidity-crunch trades around big events (Neyman), and holding rewards (3.25% on 15 markets, full-set carry) as a yield layer. Boundary: observation-feed sniping of weather is weather-markets; trading disputes themselves is rules-dispute-trading; selling sub-10c longshots across undecided events is longshot-selling-flb; crypto end-of-window entries are documented in short-crypto-latency-taker.
critic_notes: CROSS-REFERENCE the 'staking' seed to holding-rewards carry inside near-certain-bond-carry: it is the closest thing to staking on Polymarket itself (E2: ~$11.6k/day to ~48k wallets at 3.25%, ~$130M eligible value; complete-set eligibility is inferred, unverified). The orchestrator should confirm whether the owner meant UMA staking, holding rewards or both.

near-certain-bond-carry: category 'Arbitrage' is misleading. It is carry / tail-risk underwriting: break-even flip probability equals the discount (1% at 0.99), dispute rates run 0.2% (NBA) to 4.8% (geopolitics) per E3, gross edge +0.83c per dollar, and taker-side it is net negative in sports after fees (E4). Use 'Carry / risk premium'.

raw_discovery_candidates.name: 'Certainty harvesting': high-frequency buying of 95-99.9c outcomes
raw_discovery_candidates.one_line: Buy outcomes that are effectively decided but not yet resolved, many times a day, recycle capital by selling at 99c, dump dead positions at 0.1-0.5c.
raw_discovery_candidates.mechanism: A 1,000-wallet pattern study names this the 'Certainty Harvester': entries at $0.95-0.999 shortly before resolution, selling winners at $0.99 to speed capital turnover, and clearing losers at $0.001-0.005; an HN practitioner says the most consistent winner he saw 'was placing 95%+ odds many, many times a day', and Polymarket Analytics' founder lists 'consistent bonding on high-probability outcomes' as a recognised style. Because fees scale with p(1-p), a 0.98 entry in a 0.05-rate category pays ~0.1c per share, so the fee reform barely touched this style. It differs from classic resolution sniping in being breadth- and turnover-driven (hundreds of tiny edges) rather than a single oracle-gap bet.
raw_discovery_candidates.edge_source: Impatient holders and takers who want cash now; operational ability to verify 'decided' across many markets quickly.
raw_discovery_candidates.why_might_beat_market: Capital velocity: median redemption comes 182 s after resolution, and selling at 99c avoids even that wait.
raw_discovery_candidates.failure_modes: Negative skew - one reversal (disputed resolution, late VAR, data revision) erases dozens of wins; naive versions lose: entries at 0.80-0.99 in the last 60 s of 15-minute crypto markets lost 37.81%, and a 0.98-entry bot's +$84 paper profit was +$11 on-chain after slippage (2.8-3.4%), gas on small redemptions and unrealised marks.
raw_discovery_candidates.cheap_validation: Replay all markets that traded >=97c with >1 h to resolution: compute loss frequency and severity by category, and the net yield per capital-day after slippage.

raw_discovery_candidates.name: Tail-end buying of near-certain outcomes (90c+ 'bonding')
raw_discovery_candidates.one_line: Buy outcomes already priced 90-99c shortly before resolution and hold to $1.
raw_discovery_candidates.mechanism: Bots scan for contracts whose outcome is effectively decided (game nearly over, crypto window about to close, deadline passed) and lift offers at 90-99c, recycling capital many times per day. Fees barely bite at the extremes because of the p*(1-p) curve (about 0.33c per share at 95c in crypto, less elsewhere). Hard data puts the gross edge at under 1% per dollar on average, so the business is turnover, selection and avoiding the rare reversal. Open-source 'late-entry probability capture' bots for BTC 5/15-min markets are this strategy.
raw_discovery_candidates.edge_source: Impatient holders selling certainty at a discount for liquidity; fee curve near zero at extremes; time-to-resolution information.
raw_discovery_candidates.why_might_beat_market: The average is thin but positive and the capital turns fast; selection (skipping manipulable or dispute-prone markets) is where an agent can add value over the blind average.

raw_discovery_candidates.failure_modes: One reversal at 97c wipes ~30 wins; disputed/ambiguous resolutions lock capital for 4-6 days; crowded, so offers at 99c+ leave no margin after gas/relayer limits; habitual favorite-buyers underperform.
raw_discovery_candidates.cheap_validation: From the public trade archive compute realized return of all >=95c purchases made within the last N minutes before resolution, by category and time-to-close; keep only buckets with positive return after fees.

raw_discovery_candidates.name: Settlement-discount carry: post-event bonding and the near-certainty term structure
raw_discovery_candidates.one_line: Price near-certain claims as zero-coupon bonds with a venue-specific discount curve; supply exit liquidity in the resolved-but-unsettled window and avoid long-dated 'certainties' that only pay ~4-7% annualised.
raw_discovery_candidates.mechanism: After the real-world outcome is known but before oracle settlement/redemption, holders sell winning shares at 0.995-0.9995 to free capital; a bonding bot buys them and redeems. Generalise it: fit the annualised settlement wedge ASW(tau) on the 0.1-0.5 percentile frontier of near-certain prices and only buy claims whose implied yield exceeds the curve plus a dispute-risk spread. In negRisk events conversion mechanically compresses the discount (average price 1-(1-D)/(n-1)), so large fields are structurally poorer carry. Tail fees are ~0 under the p(1-p) curve.
raw_discovery_candidates.edge_source: Time value of locked collateral (Polymarket collateral earns nothing by default, unlike Kalshi's ~4% APY) plus impatience of winners who want capital back.
raw_discovery_candidates.why_might_beat_market: Hours-long holding periods make annualised returns high on the short end, and the explicit curve tells you when 'free money at 0.97' is actually below the DeFi lending rate.

evidence.title: When Certainty Is Not Worth It: Capital Lock-Up and Settlement Discounting in Prediction Markets (Gebele, Matthes), arXiv
evidence.supports: 154,298 near-certainty observations, 4,273 markets, 19.87M trades to 2025-12-31: mean ASW 4.36% (0.1-pct frontier), 6.89% (0.5-pct), min-frontier 3.06%; long-end hump at 230-260 days; bonding trades median APY 6.22%, mean 29.08%, median holding 1-2 h; top provider earned $23,616 over 34,994 trades (~0.04 c per trade); correlation with AAVE lending rate ~0.365; discount adjustment removes 47.8-87.6% of the near-certainty maturity gradient; Kalshi frontier flatter, consistent with yield-bearing collateral.

evidence.title: Resolution Is Not Settlement, Part II: Protocol Finality and Observed Redemption on Polymarket (Nechepurenko), arXiv
evidence.supports: 99,283 resolved conditions: median 182 s from protocol finality to first redemption (200 s for positive-payout), 92.8% with observed redemption at snapshot.

evidence.title: Resolution Is Not Settlement, Part I: Oracle Adjudication and Semantic Governance on Polymarket (Nechepurenko), arXiv
evidence.supports: 159,447 proposals, 1,604 disputes (1.01%), 1,478 resets; request-to-first-proposal median 182 s on legacy route vs 2-9 days on modern routes - the carry window is route-dependent and measurable on-chain.

raw_discovery_candidates.failure_modes: 1% dispute rate and reset/clarification risk is concentrated exactly in these positions; ~0.04 c per trade means scale and zero operational error are required; short-end annualised numbers are partly a tick-size artefact (0.9995 quotes).
raw_discovery_candidates.cheap_validation: Compute your own ASW frontier from public trades for the last 90 days by oracle route and category; backtest buying only above-curve claims with a haircut for dispute frequency by category (disputes cluster in sports 31.5%, politics 20.4%, crypto 16.7% per arXiv 2604.15674).

raw_discovery_candidates.name: Liquidity-crunch / time-value trades
raw_discovery_candidates.one_line: Sell patience: buy positions that impatient or cash-hungry traders dump (long-dated futures, near-certain NOs), or pre-position in absurd YES ahead of predictable cash demand.
raw_discovery_candidates.mechanism: Capital on Polymarket earns 0% and is scarce around big events, so long-dated and near-certain positions trade at discounts. The sports MM reports long-dated team futures 'trading 40% below fair value compared to sharp sportsbooks' because nobody wants months of exposure - buy there and hedge at a book. Neyman documents the mirror image: before the 2024 election NO-holders dumped safe positions for cash, forgoing ~16% annualised, and YES on the 'Jesus returns' market went 0.3% -> 1.5% (5x); YES buyers were betting on that future cash demand. A small example: Maduro-back NO at 11% for a 10.6% return in <11 months.
raw_discovery_candidates.edge_source: Being the unconstrained holder of capital when others are liquidity-constrained; term-structure of 'boring' probabilities.
raw_discovery_candidates.why_might_beat_market: No native leverage/yield on most positions makes time preference a priced factor that a patient, hedged book can harvest.
raw_discovery_candidates.failure_modes: Opportunity cost vs T-bills (~3.6% cited), platform/oracle/collateral (pUSD) risk over long horizons, hedge-leg limits at sportsbooks, rule changes that add yield on positions (unverified whether holding rewards currently apply).
raw_discovery_candidates.cheap_validation: Track a basket of 95c+ long-dated NOs and their implied annualised yields weekly; test whether yields spike into major events (midterms Nov 2026) as predicted.

raw_discovery_candidates.name: Holding-rewards carry on full sets and eligible inventory
raw_discovery_candidates.one_line: Earn the 3.25% annualised holding reward on position value in 15 eligible long-dated markets, including on risk-free YES+NO full sets, as a yield layer under market-making inventory.
raw_discovery_candidates.mechanism: Effective 2026-06-01 Polymarket pays 3.25% annualised (variable, at its discretion, may be capped) on total position value in 15 listed markets: 2028 presidential/nomination markets, 2026 midterms, five 'leader out before 2027' markets, Russia-Ukraine ceasefire before 2027 and five 2026 crypto price markets. Position value is sampled at a random time each hour and counts both YES and NO shares at mid price, so splitting pUSD into a YES+NO full set yields about $1 of reward-bearing value with no market risk and can be merged back at any time (gasless through the relayer). The same full-set inventory can back ask-only quotes on both outcomes, so it simultaneously earns holding reward, liquidity rewards and, in fee-enabled markets such as the 2028 nominee markets (feeRate 0.04), maker rebates. A migration to a new rewards system with 1-click migration is announced for later in 2026.
raw_discovery_candidates.edge_source: Subsidy on capital that would otherwise sit idle on-platform; it also offsets the time-value cost that keeps 95-99c long-dated near-certainties underpriced.
raw_discovery_candidates.why_might_beat_market: It is not alpha on its own (3.25% is at or below cash yields); the value is stacking: inventory that is already required for quoting earns carry, and carry-adjusted fair value for long-dated NO positions differs from what non-eligible holders compute.
raw_discovery_candidates.failure_modes: Rate already cut (was higher before June 2026) and can be cut or capped again; only 15 markets; smart-contract and platform custody risk on parked capital (two security incidents in May-June 2026); opportunity cost versus off-platform yield.
raw_discovery_candidates.cheap_validation: Split $1,000 into a full set on one eligible market for a week and reconcile daily pUSD credits against 3.25%/365 x $1,000; confirm both legs are counted.
